Bologna on foot

Wizzy knows 43 places in Bologna, from the big sights to the corners most people walk straight past. Start a walk, put your phone away, and Wizzy taps you on the shoulder when there's something worth looking up at.

WIZZYnow
Basilica of San Petronio

A vast Gothic church whose façade is only half clad in marble.

{% include appstore-badge.html ct="web-bologna" %}

The must-sees

  • Archiginnasio

    Culture · 1563

    Built in 1563, it was the first single seat of the university. Its wooden Anatomical Theatre was destroyed by bombing in 1944 and rebuilt from the original pieces.

    Look for: In the Anatomical Theatre, two wooden skinned men, the Spellati, hold up the canopy over the lecturer’s chair.

  • Basilica of San Petronio

    Church

    Building began in 1390 and the façade was never finished. A long meridian line set into the floor by the astronomer Giovanni Domenico Cassini in the 1650s still marks noon with a beam of sunlight.

    Look for: Around the central door, Jacopo della Quercia’s stone reliefs tell Genesis, from the creation of Adam to Noah.

  • Fountain of Neptune

    Landmark

    Giambologna made the bronze figures in the 1560s for a papal project to beautify the city. Locals call the statue simply il Gigante, the Giant.

    Look for: On the town hall wall facing the fountain, rows of photographs remember the partisans of Bologna killed in the Second World War.

  • Piazza Maggiore

    Square

    It has been the centre of city life since the Middle Ages. In summer it becomes an open-air cinema in front of San Petronio.

    Look for: Under the vault beneath Palazzo del Podestà, two people whispering into opposite corners can hear each other clearly across the space.

  • Sanctuary of San Luca

    Church

    The portico has 666 arches, built with money from the city’s families and guilds. Every year an image of the Madonna is carried down to the cathedral and back.

    Look for: Where the portico leaves the plain and starts to climb, it crosses the road on the Meloncello arch, a curved Baroque bridge.

  • Santo Stefano

    Church

    Known as the Seven Churches, the complex grew over many centuries around a round church modelled on the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. The cloister and courtyards connect them.

    Look for: In the open courtyard, find the large stone basin called Pilate’s Basin. It is an 8th-century Lombard piece, linked to Pilate only by legend.

  • Two Towers

    Landmark

    Rich families built dozens of towers in medieval Bologna, and these two from the 12th century are the best known. The Asinelli is close to 100 metres tall; the shorter Garisenda leans hard.

    Look for: Look up at the Garisenda from the street and follow its lean. It was cut down in the 14th century because it tilted so far.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Bologna and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Bologna passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
